### Adr Drafter

1 ADR(s); 1 accepted.

**Client-side idempotency key for payment retries** — _accepted_
- Context: Payment requests require idempotent retries to prevent duplicate charges. Two options were evaluated: (A) the client sends a dedupe/idempotency key with every payment request and the gateway rejects a repeat within 24 hours; (B) a server-side dedupe table keyed on merchant, amount, and a time window. Option B was rejected because it would incorrectly block two legitimate payments of the same amount within the window.
- Decision: Adopt Option A: all clients send an idempotency key header with each payment request; the gateway rejects a second request carrying the same key for 24 hours. The server-side dedupe table will not be built.
- Consequences: All four existing clients must be updated to send the key; the mobile client has a two-week release cycle, so full coverage takes several weeks. Rollout order: web client first, then mobile in the release after next (Mira owns the rollout plan). Theo will update the reconciliation job to read the idempotency key. Support team will be notified that duplicate charges will cease after the mobile release (stakeholder update owned by Me). Jun to formalize this ADR by Wednesday.

- No server-side dedupe table (Option B) will be built; idempotency is handled solely via the client-supplied key.
- An ADR documenting the idempotent-retry decision must be written by Wednesday.
- Rollout order: web client first, then mobile client in the release after next.
- Mobile client release cadence is every two weeks, which bounds the earliest date duplicate charges stop for mobile users.

**Acceptance criteria**
- After the mobile client release ships, duplicate charges must no longer occur.

The team chose Option A (client-side dedupe key) over Option B (server dedupe table) due to the risk of blocking legitimate duplicate-amount payments and the gateway's existing idempotency key support.
